provision: Qualifying late wage, due/paid dates and governing bank rate → statutory delay compensation
citation: Labour Code 45/2019/QH14 (consolidation 18/VBHN-VPQH of 12 Feb 2026) art.97; whole scope
reason: Unproven (re-judged 2026-09-30; was VERIFIED 2026-09-29): the under-15-day no-compensation branch and the force-majeure branch until the test phase runs the workers added to VN-LC97-01-1 on 2026-09-30 (xuyen_job paid 14 days late → none; xoan2_job force majeure → 49,316). Proven: a 20-day delay at a stated bank rate (xuan_job). History: No amount or rate-history mechanism for established qualifying delay. Art.97(4) (Gazette text, 2026-09-28): a force-majeure delay may not exceed **30 days**; a delay of **15 days or more** earns at least interest at the payroll bank's **1-month term-deposit rate** on the payment date. The threshold, ceiling, force-majeure predicate and bank-rate source are not saved inputs. Round 3 (2026-09-28): not seedable — the rate is the payroll bank's own published 1-month rate on the payment date (per employer, per day, not a jurisdiction constant), and the engine has no wage due-date/paid-date pair outside final pay (`FINAL_PAY_LATE` is a warning only); art.97(4) also sets no day-count basis for “số tiền lãi”, an owner decision. Recorded as an engine defect. Engine defect fixed (2026-09-28): an ad hoc request now records `late_wage` (due day, paid day, the payroll bank's published 1-month rate with its notice, force majeure; the request amount is the late sum), and a band reads `entry.late_wage.days`/`.deposit_rate`/`.force_majeure` (fixture test in `statutory-golden-vn.test.ts`). Round 4 (2026-09-28), closed: Decree 145/2020/ND-CP (Official Gazette 1203+1204) carries no rule of its own (its only art.97(4) mention is the domestic worker's no-notice resignation exception, art.89(1)(d)(d1), Gazette 1203+1204 p.79; art.55 is overtime pay), so the owner rule applies. **Owner rule 2026-09-28: law silent on the day count; default actual days over a 365-day year, days = paid day − due day, rounded up to the whole đồng; lawful because it is the State Bank's own rule for deposit interest (Circular 14/2017/TT-NHNN art.4(1): a rate is % a year, a year is 365 days; art.4(2)(a): first day out, last day in) and rounding up never pays below the art.97(4) minimum.** **Owner rule 2026-09-28: law silent on a delay without force majeure (the compensation sits in the force-majeure sentence); default the same compensation for any delay of 15 days or more; lawful because art.97(4) sets a minimum (“ít nhất”) and nothing forbids paying it; the sanction remedy for an unlawful delay (VN-D12-03, VN-D283-04) is separate and not replaced.** **Owner rule 2026-09-28: law silent on PIT/SI treatment; default taxable salary income (counts toward PIT), outside SI/HI/UI (not a regular wage item, Decree 158/2025/ND-CP art.7(1)); lawful because withholding on a receipt from the employer is corrected at finalisation, while no exemption naming it was found (exemption lists not exhaustively re-read).** Seeded `LATE_WAGE_COMPENSATION` (MANUAL, PAY/ADD, band `entry.late_wage.days >= 15`, `round(amount × rate/100 × days/365, 1, 'UP')`) in all four live versions — a missing rule of unchanged law, fixed in place. The 30-day force-majeure ceiling is a conduct limit, not an amount; not enforced (sourced exclusion). Golden: August wages 20,000,000 due 10 September 2026, paid 28 September (18 days) at Vietcombank's published 2.10% 1-month rate of 28/09/2026 → 20,713, with and without force majeure; paid 24 September (14 days) → none. Closure case: One qualifying and one excluded delay, using dated bank rate. R27. Source note (Circular 14/2017/TT-NHNN): Official Gazette 793+794 of 23 October 2017 (text layer), in force 1 January 2018; art.4(1) % a year on 365 days, art.4(2)(a)/(b) day count; congbao lists no amending instrument (checked 2026-09-28). Golden input (not seed law): Vietcombank retail VND deposit rates https://www.vietcombank.com.vn/vi-VN/KHCN/Cong-cu-tien-ich/KHCN---Lai-suat, 1 month 2.10% a year, table updated 09:31 28/09/2026, actual days on a 365-day basis. Golden: the 15 September 2026 leaver, 60,000,000 × 11 ÷ 22 = 30,000,000 (VN-LC46-01), and the 15 July non-resident, 46,000,000 × 11 ÷ 23. Engine defect fixed 2026-09-28: `employment_terms.proration` (optional, dated by the row) is the contract's own basis — CALENDAR_DAYS, WORKING_DAYS or FIXED_DAYS n — and `work_rules.proration_contractual: true` (all 23 VN versions; a missing rule of unchanged law, fixed in place) lets it replace the version's basis for that row, on the salary segment, an absence and an allowance's part period alike; absent, the working-day default applies. The floors are untouched: the minimum-wage check reads the contract month and `ordinary_divisor_days` stays `period.working_days`. Golden (statutory-golden-vn, January 2026 joiner on the 19th): 22,000,000 × 13 ÷ 31 = 9,225,806 (calendar), × 10 ÷ 26 = 8,461,538 (26), a whole month on 26 = 22,000,000, a 5,000,000 contract on 26 still blocks at Region I's 5,310,000, and a version without the flag ignores the contract basis (10 ÷ 22). Closure case: Mid-month joiner under two contractual divisors, minimum-wage check and 13/14 unpaid days.
